![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094599/assets/f813b6460f60a2fb6daf53c9fef61f47a8961137842e282418da398ba7873d48.png)

Find the differential equation governing the current $I$ (in amperes) at time $t$ (in seconds) in the circuit given in the diagram above.

*Hint: The voltage drop ${V}_{C}$ across the capacitor is related to its charge by $q=C{V}_{C},$ where $C$ is the capacitance measured in Farads.*
worked_solution:
The diagram shows a series RCL circuit with a source electromotive force (EMF) of $15\,\text{V},$ a resistor of resistance $30\,Ω,$ a capacitor of capacitance $0.002\,\text{F},$ and an inductor of inductance $6\,\text{H}.$

The current $I,$ measured in amperes, is defined as the rate of flow of charge $q,$ measured in coulombs.

$$
I=\frac{dq}{dt}
$$

Kirchhoff's voltage law states that in a series circuit, the source voltage (EMF) equals the sum of the voltage drops.

In an RCL circuit, there are three voltage drops:

- The voltage drop across the resistor is proportional to the current, with a constant of proportionality $R=30\,Ω.$ So,

$$
{V}_{R}=30I.
$$

- The voltage drop across the capacitor is related to its charge by $q=C{V}_{C}.$ Therefore,

$$
{V}_{C}=\frac{q}{C}=\frac{q}{0.002}=500q.
$$

- The voltage drop across the inductor is proportional to the rate of change of current, with a constant of proportionality $L=6\,\text{H}.$ Hence,

$$
{V}_{L}=6\,\frac{dI}{dt}.
$$

Therefore, by Kirchhoff's voltage law, these values are related by the equation

$$
15=30I+500q+6\,\frac{dI}{dt}.
$$

Differentiating with respect to $t,$ the differential equation governing the current in the circuit is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{d}{dt}(15) & =\frac{d}{dt}(30I+500q+6\,\frac{dI}{dt}) \\ 0 & =30\,\frac{dI}{dt}+500\,\frac{dq}{dt}+6\,\frac{{d}^{2}I}{d{t}^{2}},\end{aligned}
$$

which, when substituting in $I=\frac{dq}{dt},$ gives

$$
\frac{{d}^{2}I}{d{t}^{2}}+5\,\frac{dI}{dt}+\frac{250}{3}I=0.
$$
